name: Predominantly Medium-Vessel Vasculitis

criteria.description: Evidence of vasculitis predominantly affecting medium-sized arteries confirmed by angiography or histopathology
Presence of clinical signs consistent with medium-vessel vasculitis such as livedo reticularis, nodules, ulcers, or ischemic symptoms
Exclusion of small-vessel and large-vessel vasculitis by clinical, laboratory, and imaging criteria
Elevated acute phase reactants such as ESR or CRP

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of medium-vessel involvement confirmed by imaging or biopsy plus compatible clinical features and exclusion of other vasculitides
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation and exclusion of mimics.

pathognomonic.notes: Mottled, net-like vascular pattern on the skin
Detected by angiography, characteristic of medium-vessel involvement

common.notes: Mononeuritis multiplex or distal sensory loss
Muscle and joint pain without swelling

occasional.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
occasional.notes: Due to renal artery stenosis or ischemia
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys
belly pain from poor blood flow
abdominal pain due to intestinal ischemia
systemic symptoms like malaise and fever

occasional.notes: Vasospasm of small arteries and arterioles

rare.symptomName: Cardiac ischemia due to coronary artery involvement
searchTerms: chest pain due to coronary artery disease
angina from heart blood flow problems

rare.notes: Rare involvement of cerebral medium-sized arteries
searchTerms: central nervous system blood flow loss
brain tissue death from blocked vessels

imaging: Angiographic evidence of segmental arterial aneurysms and stenoses in medium-sized vessels
MRI or CT angiography showing vessel wall inflammation
other: Histopathology showing transmural inflammation with fibrinoid necrosis in medium-sized arteries

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic necrotizing vasculitis with medium-sized artery involvement
Often associated with hepatitis B infection
More frequent renal and gastrointestinal involvement
Small to medium vessel vasculitis with granulomatous inflammation
Upper and lower respiratory tract involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of ischemic ulcers or gangrene
New onset hypertension with renal artery stenosis
Signs of organ ischemia such as mesenteric or cardiac ischemia
references: Jennette JC et al. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013 Jan;65(1):1-11.
